claims.text: The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust appointed retired Air Marshal Jeetendra Mishra as its first Chief Executive Officer.
The Shri Ram Janmabhoomi Teerth Kshetra Trust appointed Govind Dev Giri as its General Secretary, succeeding Champat Rai.
The Trust selected retired Air Marshal Jeetendra Mishra from a shortlist of three candidates after evaluating 5,585 applications for the CEO post.
The Trust appointed Mahesh Bhagchandka as treasurer and inducted Madan Mohan Pandey, Mahesh Bhagchandka, and Dr Nirmala Yadav as new trustees.
Retired Air Marshal Jeetendra Mishra commanded the Indian Air Force's Western Air Command during Operation Sindoor and was awarded the Sarvottam Yudh Seva Medal.
Former General Secretary Champat Rai and trustee Anil Mishra resigned on moral grounds on June 26 following allegations of donation embezzlement.
A preliminary report by Uttar Pradesh's Special Investigation Team on June 23 found 70 instances of counting staff hiding cash in their clothing and shoes at the Ram temple.
Retired Air Marshal Jeetendra Mishra stated that he learned about his appointment as CEO through television news broadcasts.
Retired Air Marshal Jeetendra Mishra served in the Indian Air Force for nearly 39 years prior to his retirement.
Retired Air Marshal Jeetendra Mishra retired from the Indian Air Force on April 30, 2026.
India's former Chief Economic Adviser stated that the double deflator methodology provides a better approach for calculating GDP.
Union Minister Piyush Goyal stated that ministers do not manufacture data and asserted that India's 7.8 percent GDP growth figure is real.
According to MoSPI data released on August 31, India's real GDP grew 7.8 percent in Q1 FY27, with real GDP estimated at Rs 81.36 lakh crore.
India's nominal GDP reached Rs 88.27 lakh crore in Q1 FY27, up 10.3 percent from Rs 80 lakh crore in Q1 FY26.

Former Finance Secretary Subhash Garg claimed that Q1 FY27 GDP growth in current prices would have been about 2.6 percent if last year's Q1 GDP had not been revised down from roughly Rs 86 lakh crore to Rs 80 lakh crore.

MoSPI stated that Q1 FY26 GDP was initially estimated at Rs 86.05 lakh crore under the 2011-12 base year, but was revised to Rs 80.32 lakh crore after introducing the 2022-23 base year series in February 2026.
Sanjeev Sanyal, a member of the Prime Minister's Economic Advisory Council, stated that updating the GDP base year to 2022-23 was delayed due to the Covid-19 pandemic.

Congress leader Jairam Ramesh criticized the GDP calculations as statistical gymnastics, citing a gap between implied GDP inflation of 2.3 percent and wholesale price index inflation exceeding 9 percent.
SBI Group Chief Economic Adviser Soumya Kanti Ghosh spoke to NDTV regarding doubts raised about India's GDP growth data.
India's Ministry of External Affairs condemned the reported destruction of a century-old Hindu temple in village Siraj, Narowal district, Pakistan.
MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal called the temple destruction a reprehensible act of vandalism and requested Pakistani authorities to conduct a transparent investigation and restore the structure.

Minority rights group Pakistan Masiha Millat Party alleged the Narowal temple was deliberately demolished to expand an adjacent seminary, while Pakistan's Evacuee Trust Property Board stated it collapsed due to heavy rainfall.
The destroyed Hindu temple in Siraj village was demolished on August 21 and was estimated to be 100 to 125 years old.
Pakistan Masiha Millat Party chairman Aslam Parvez Sahotra approached authorities seeking legal action against those responsible for destroying the temple.
As of Wednesday, 16,784 people were evacuated to safety due to persistent flood conditions across 23 affected districts in Uttar Pradesh.
Three people died in rain-related incidents in Uttar Pradesh, including an 18-month-old child in Pratapgarh and two men aged 32 and 55 in Amroha.
Uttar Pradesh deployed 1,499 boats and 1,067 medical teams to support flood relief operations across affected districts.
Cumulative rainfall during the southwest monsoon season across India was 13 percent below normal as of September 2, standing at 618.5 mm against the normal 714.3 mm.
All 69 gates of the Sone Barrage at Indrapuri in Bihar were opened on Wednesday to facilitate a water discharge of 5.59 lakh cusecs.
Major rivers in Bihar, including the Kosi, Gandak, Burhi Gandak, Ganga, and Punpun, flowed above danger marks at multiple locations.
